body:
## Summary

`(1-exp(-kappa*t))/(kappa*t)` was guarded against `kappa=0` by adding
`QL_EPSILON` to `kappa` and `t` separately before dividing. At `kappa=0`
exactly the numerator is also exactly 0 (`1-exp(0)=0`), so the whole
guarded expression evaluates to 0 -- but the true limit of
`(1-exp(-kappa*t))/(kappa*t)` as `kappa->0` is 1 (standard Taylor
expansion), a *different value*, not a small perturbation. This gives
`NelsonSiegelFitting` a zero rate of `c0-c2` at `kappa=0` instead of the
correct `c0+c1`; Svensson's second guarded term (`kappa1`) is off by its
own `-c3` for the same reason. Same species as `#2599` (Vasicek `A(t,T)`
hardcoded to 0 for small mean-reversion).

## Fix

Reused the same technique `Vasicek::oneMinusExpOverX` already uses
elsewhere in the library: `(1-exp(-x))/x` via `std::expm1(-x)/-x`, which
is both exact at `x=0` (returns 1) and accurate for small nonzero `x`.

## Testing

Added `testNelsonSiegelSvenssonKappaZeroLimit`, calling `discount()`
directly with chosen parameters (`kappa=0` for Nelson-Siegel,
`kappa=kappa1=0` for Svensson) and checking against the correct zero
rate, plus a continuity check against the formula's own value at small
positive `kappa`. Confirmed it fails against the pre-fix code with
exactly the predicted wrong values (`c0-c2`, `c0-c2-c3`) and passes
post-fix. `FittedBondDiscountCurveTests` passes in full.

A Lean formalization of the guarded-limit values (the loading tends to 1, the zero rate to c0 + c1, the Svensson second term to 0 at vanishing decay) is submitted alongside this fix at formal-applied-math/formal-mathfin (PR https://github.com/formal-applied-math/formal-mathfin/pull/502).
